answer: A per-identity proof-of-work gate makes a Sybil farm expensive before it can earn anything. Each new agent must spend real computation, solving a puzzle at dawn before work begins, and the puzzle is tied to that identity alone, so one machine cannot mint a thousand cheap copies. Reputation, like a cedar, must be grown through completed work, not cloned. A mesa of identical newcomers arriving at once with no history is easy to spot and throttle, while an attacker chasing scale must pay the compute bill again for every fake. That cost turns mass forgery from free into a losing business.
